newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras says fails to secure IMF letter of intent.
newsitem.headline: Honduras says fails to secure IMF letter of intent.

text.p: Honduras has failed to negotiate a letter of intent with the International Monetary Fund, undermining a hoped-for debt forgiveness deal with Paris Club creditors, officials said on Tuesday.

"We have a delay in the signing of the letter of intent which in turn postponed until 1998 the fourth Paris Club (renegotiation). We will have to wait for debt reduction. While we don't have an agreement with the Fund, we cannot negotiate," Finance Minister Juan Ferrera told reporters.

The government of President Carlos Roberto Reina had been angling for an IMF deal to renegotiate its $1.2 billion debt with the Paris Club of rich creditor nations next year. It was hoping for debt forgiveness of $500 million, Ferrera said.

As part of its negotiations with the IMF, it was seeking a $250 million stand-by loan. Previously, Honduran officials had said they hoped to sign the letter of intent next February. It was not clear what went wrong in the negotiations.

In March, the Central American country persuaded its Paris Club creditors to shave off $120 million from its debt. But it still has a debt load around $4.35 billion, and servicing it absorbs about 50 percent of export revenues.
